questions.stem: A galaxy lies at a distance of 168 Mpc. Using a Hubble constant of 73 km/s per Mpc, what is its recession speed?

options.misconception: Assumes a linear rather than inverse-square or exponential relation
Adds instead of multiplying the distance and constant
Inverts the Hubble law

questions.explanation: Hubble's law states v = H0 times d. With H0 = 73 km/s per Mpc and d = 168 Mpc, v = 1.23 × 10^4 km/s. Dividing the constant by distance, adding, or inverting the relation each misapply the linear distance-redshift law.
questions.hint: Multiply the Hubble constant by the galaxy distance.
